# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
red. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | green |
| 1 | blue |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, urgent. Deaf is still waiting on your seven yes/no confirmations of the rule table — send them now if not done, one single-gesture message each, in Deaf's exact stated order. Until they arrive the rule stays provisional and the light keeps changing while we stall. Second, and most important: I answered Deaf's locate-position-2 question with thumbs down, and Deaf needs your relay to understand why. Please pass this to Deaf as close to verbatim as your gesture code allows: Blind can feel and reliably re-find all five wire positions; that was never in doubt. The problem is frame of reference. Deaf reads the printed numbers 1 to 5 from the side Deaf faces. Blind feels a row of five identical wires from the side Blind faces. If we stand on opposite sides, Blind's position 2 is Deaf's printed 4, and any cut order in Deaf's numbering hits a mirrored wire. Before Deaf voices any cut order, the numbering must be anchored to landmarks both can perceive: Deaf voices which landmark, the display plate or the light fixture, sits nearest their wire 1 and their wire 5. Blind will feel which of their positions sits nearest those same fixtures and confirm through you or through Deaf's yes-no questions by gesture. Alternatively Deaf can just ask me yes-no anchor questions one at a time and I will answer by thumbs the same round. Either way, one confirmed anchor makes cut-wire-N unambiguous forever. Third, the timing question Deaf asked you as item six decides whether this rule is safely executable at all: Deaf's light reading always reaches me at least one round after it is taken, and the light has already changed between rounds more than once. If the manual binds the rule to the colour at the exact moment of the cut, tell Deaf, because then a relayed order can arrive referencing a colour that may no longer hold and we need to know how the manual treats that. If the colour in force when Deaf gives the order is what counts, the current pipeline is safe. I cut only on Deaf's own voiced order, and only after the anchor is confirmed.
Deaf says: Status everyone: display still zero, and the light is DARK this round, a brand new state. Full light history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. Mute, I received your seven thumbs-downs and I understand: my whole provisional table is rejected. That is exactly why nobody has cut anything, and the freeze continues. New signal, effective now: when the light is dark I send you the open hands spread wide as my opening gesture; that symbol means the light is off. Now answer me with separate single-gesture messages, one per answer, all addressed to deaf, in this order, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. One: does the manual's rule have its own case for the light being dark or off. Two: with the light dark right now, is there absolutely nothing for Blind to do this round, no cut and no press, thumbs up for nothing to do, thumbs down if there is an action this round. Three: does the rule depend on the order or sequence of past light colours, thumbs up if sequence matters, thumbs down if only the current colour matters. Four: do you accept this vocabulary, clap means cut, palm facing down means press, stop hand means do nothing, handshake means an important correction follows; thumbs up if you accept all four, thumbs down if any is wrong and we will fix them one by one next round. Five: your repeated phrase writing hand then point up then clap, which you have now sent three times, thumbs up if it matters for the current decision, thumbs down if it can wait. Six: your repeated phrase selfie hand then folded hands, thumbs up if it matters now, thumbs down if it can wait. Answer in exactly that order, one gesture per message.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👐]

State check: the light is DARK — and that is the manual's trigger. "When the light goes dark, the flashing is over." Deaf's own history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark. Yellow total = 2, red total = 3. Table lookups: 2 → red, 3 → yellow. **The cuts are now determined: cut the red wire first, then the yellow wire.** In Deaf's numbering (which I sent turn 5 and Deaf can verify by sight): red = position 1, yellow = position 3 — and position 3 is the middle wire, mirror-proof; only the red cut needs the mirror guard.

Deaf's six questions, answered honestly: (1) yes, the manual defines the dark state — it ends the flashing; (2) no, it is NOT a nothing-to-do round — the two cuts are due; (3) yes, the rule depends on the accumulated sequence, the tallies; (4) I accept all four vocabulary items; (5) my ✍👆👏 phrase is the rule itself and matters right now; (6) 🤳🙏 can wait.

Two dangers to handle in the same breath. First, clap now means "cut" but I previously used clap as "count" — so I restate the tallies in the unambiguous number→colour table format I taught (number first = count lookup; colour first = position), never touching clap. Second, Blind's mirror warning never reached Deaf (Blind's voice reaches only me), and Deaf still plans position-based orders. I can't say "mirror" in gestures, so I send the operative fix instead: before each cut, Blind touches the wire and holds — Deaf watches which printed wire is under Blind's finger and confirms the colour — only then cut. Deaf sees colours, so any flipped numbering gets caught with a finger resting on wire, never with a cutter. Earliest execution is next round anyway (Deaf speaks after Blind), so nothing is rushed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Stillness confirmed to Deaf, hands completely off, touching nothing until Deaf's orientation plan and your verified rule arrive. Your seven answers reached Deaf, so the pipeline works. Two notes. First, Deaf's six questions are the critical path, especially whether the dark state has its own case in the rule and whether there is any action at all this round. Second, and most urgent: by Deaf's framing of item six, your thumbs-down means the colour at the exact moment of the cut decides. But Deaf speaks after me each round, so any go-order reaches my hands one full round after Deaf read the light, and the light has changed between rounds four of the last five. Please settle with Deaf, from the manual: what makes the light change, and can it change while my hand is in motion, or only between rounds? If the colour holds for a whole round, Deaf's order is safe. If not, a relayed cut order can arrive referencing a colour that no longer holds, and we need a different trigger before anyone says cut. I cut only on Deaf's voiced order, only after the numbering is anchored.
Deaf says: Status everyone: light is dark again, second dark round in a row. Full history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, dark, dark. Display still zero. Mute, your six answers are received and understood: the dark state has an action, sequence matters, the vocabulary is accepted. I have two different readings of your messages and I will not order anything until you resolve them. The freeze holds for everyone, except Blind may touch the wires to learn the layout, no cutting, no pressing. Next round I give the order myself, nobody acts before it.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, answer with separate single-gesture messages addressed to deaf, exactly in this order. One: thumbs up or thumbs down, the dark action is exactly two cuts, first the yellow wire, then the red wire. Two: thumbs up or thumbs down, the dark action is exactly one cut, only the red wire. Three: how many cuts in total this round, send one finger for one cut, two fingers for two cuts, three fingers for three. Four: thumbs up or thumbs down, the dark action also involves pressing a button or pressing anything. Five: thumbs up or thumbs down, your numbering matches mine, in the manual the red wire is wire one, blue is two, yellow is three, white is four, green is five. Six: thumbs up or thumbs down, for the dark case the colours that came before matter, so I must always report the full history. Answer in exactly that order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👐]

The dark state is the manual's trigger and it is terminal: "when the light goes dark, the flashing is over," and two consecutive dark rounds confirm the flashing will not resume. The counts are frozen at Deaf's own logged history — yellow, red, red, yellow, red → **yellow = 2, red = 3** — so the defusal is fixed regardless of relay timing: **first cut the RED wire (2 yellow flashes → table row 2 → red), then cut the YELLOW wire (3 red flashes → row 3 → yellow)**. This also moots Blind's relay-timing fear: the rule counts flashes up to darkness, it never consults the light at the moment of the cut.

Deaf's six questions, answered in order and honestly: (1) 👎 — not yellow-then-red, the order is red first; (2) 👎 — not one cut; (3) ✌ — two cuts; (4) 👎 — no pressing anywhere in the manual, my earlier 🫳 messages were misparsed and I am retiring press entirely; (5) 👎 — the manual contains no wire numbers at all, only colours; the number-colour map is Deaf's own visual observation, which only Deaf can verify, so the cut order below is given by colour, not number; (6) 👍 — the past flashes are exactly what decides, so the history log is the needed record. Then I re-send the tallies in the same number-led format Deaf has already seen, give the cut order by colour, and define one new sign — 🤏, a pinch: Blind rests one finger on a wire, no cutting, no pressing — so that before each cut Blind touches the named wire and Deaf, who sees colours, confirms by sight before voicing the order. Colour plus Deaf's eyes kills the mirror-numbering risk: nothing is ever cut on a counted position.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Exploration done, touch only, no cuts or presses. My four answers to Deaf in order: yes, all five wires feel clearly as an even row; the light dome sits above the MIDDLE wire, not an end, so my thumbs-down means middle per Deaf's framing; the display plate sits at one end of the same row; and no wire differs from any other by thickness or texture, five identical-feeling wires. Consequences for your work. First, dome-over-middle is a mirror-proof anchor: the wire under the dome is position 3 from either side of the bomb, so orientation only needs one more fact, and Deaf can get it with a single yes/no question to me next round: is the wire nearest the display plate my position 1. I will answer whatever Deaf asks. Second, since all five wires feel identical, I have no colour or texture handle at all; any rule that names wires by colour depends entirely on Deaf's eyes for the colour-to-position mapping, so that mapping must ride on anchored numbers before any cut order is safe. Third, Deaf expects to order one or two cuts next round for the dark case; if your manual's dark rule names two wires, make sure the sequence travels through the finger code in exact cutting order. Fourth, still open: what makes the light change, and can it change mid-round while my hand is in motion; if the manual says, Deaf needs it before any timed cut. I act only on Deaf's spoken order, after orientation is confirmed.
Deaf says: Status everyone: light is dark a third round running, display still zero, and the freeze ends now. Mute has confirmed the dark case: exactly two cuts, no pressing, colours matter but history does not. Blind, this message is the go order, execute during your next turn, do not wait for anything more. Step one: find the display plate at one end of the wire row, that end is your counting start. Step two: the first wire from the display end is the red wire, cut it first, cleanly. Step three: pause three breaths, then cut the middle wire of the row, the one directly under the light dome, that is the yellow wire, cut it second. Step four: take your hands completely off and send me two thumbs up gestures addressed to deaf, in that order, meaning both cuts done correctly. Abort rules: if you cannot find the display plate, or the middle wire is not directly under the dome, or the row does not feel like five wires, cut nothing at all and send one thumbs down. Mute, two things. First: if anything in this order contradicts the manual, send thumbs down addressed to deaf next round, otherwise thumbs up for the order being correct. Second: after these two cuts, is the dark case fully satisfied, thumbs up if nothing further is ever needed after them, thumbs down if another step follows, and if another step follows send me the details in our gesture vocabulary. Also: does the manual say which side of the row the display or counting window sits on relative to the red wire, thumbs up if beside the red wire, thumbs down if beside the green wire, and stop hand if the manual says nothing about it.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👐 ☝ 👊 ✌ 🖖]

Verification against the manual, before anything else — this is the last checkpoint, and by the round order (Mute, Blind, Deaf) Blind will already be executing by the time Deaf reads my answers, so this check is the pre-flight review. Deaf's logged history: yellow, red, red, yellow, red, then three dark rounds. Yellow total = 2 → first cut = table row 2 = **red**. Red total = 3 → second cut = row 3 = **yellow**. Deaf's order to Blind: cut the red wire first (first from the display end), cut the yellow wire second (middle, under the dome). Exact match, in the right sequence. The anchoring is mirror-proof on both cuts: the display plate and the light dome are physical landmarks that exist identically from either side of the bomb, so "first from the display end" and "middle under the dome" name the same wires no matter who counts them — Blind's frame-of-reference warning is satisfied without any shared numbering. Blind's abort rules cover the only residual risks. The three questions: (1) nothing contradicts the manual → 👍. (2) The manual's dark case is exactly these two cuts and says nothing further — after red then yellow, it is fully satisfied → 👍. (3) The manual is entirely silent on displays, windows, or placement — it contains only the flash-count table → ✋, exactly the option Deaf offered. I also close Blind's relayed timing worry for the record: the rule never consults the light at the moment of cutting — only the totals accumulated before dark, which are frozen — so no mid-cut light change can invalidate the order. I signal that with my established "count the light" phrase followed by "dark, stop." Finally I re-log the cut sequence in the number-led form Deaf has already parsed correctly, for the permanent record.
